aspect: Diacritics are dropped and tone is lost
description: Yoruba names carry tonal marks that most systems cannot store. Ọlámidé becomes Olamide, and the version on the passport becomes the only lawful spelling of a name that was never spelled that way.
energy_note: The official version of your name is the one the computer could manage.

description: Airline fields cap at around 30 characters. A full name of four parts is silently cut, and the truncated form then does not match the passport at check-in.
energy_note: Your name, shortened by a character limit, at the gate.

aspect: Which part is the surname is not obvious
description: Staff unfamiliar with the convention enter the wrong field, producing records where the given name and family name are swapped - across a bank, an employer and a university, differently each time.
energy_note: Filed under your first name in three databases.

description: A name change on marriage must be propagated across every registry separately. Any registry not updated produces a mismatch that is treated as the woman's error rather than the system's.
energy_note: Married, and now inconsistent everywhere at once.

description: Inconsistent names produce background-check mismatches, payroll failures, credit file fragmentation and benefit refusals long after any immigration question is settled.
energy_note: A transcription from 2011, still failing checks in 2026.

aspect: SCENARIO - the certificate that is not hers
description: Her WAEC certificate reads ADEYEMI Folasade Aduke. Her degree reads Folashade Adeyemi. Her passport reads Folasade Aduke ADEYEMI. The credential evaluator returns all three as unverifiable pending a sworn affidavit of one and the same person, which costs money and six weeks.
energy_note: Three documents, one woman, six weeks.
